title: 赴英留学生的残酷现实（1）
desc: 赴英留学生的残酷现实（1）

paragraphs.en: When Sam started looking into studying abroad, it didn't take long for his phone to start ringing. At 24, he was living with his parents in a small city in the eastern Indian state of Odisha and he'd been stuck in an entry-level job for four years.
paragraphs.zh: 当萨姆开始考虑出国留学时，他的电话很快就响个不停。24岁的他和父母一起住在印度东部奥里萨邦的一个小城市，一份初级工作他已经干了四年。

paragraphs.en: He hoped a master's degree in the UK might lead to a high-flying finance job in London, or at least give him an edge when he came back home.
paragraphs.zh: 他希望英国的硕士学位能帮助他在伦敦获得一份高飞的金融工作，或者至少在他回国时能让他更有竞争力。

paragraphs.en: After filling in a few forms on study abroad websites, Sam soon started receiving calls from unknown numbers. Eventually, he answered one. The person on the phone was an education agent – a recruiter who helps students apply to foreign universities – pitching his services.
paragraphs.zh: 在几个留学网站上填写了一些表格后，萨姆很快就开始接到陌生号码的来电。最终，他接了一个。电话那头是一名教育中介——帮助学生申请外国大学的招生人员——在推销他的服务。

paragraphs.en: The offer sounded appealing. The agency would help Sam decide which universities to apply to, advising on the most suitable courses and where he had the best chance of admission.
paragraphs.zh: 这个提议听起来很诱人。该中介机构将帮助萨姆决定申请哪些大学，就最合适的课程以及他最有希望被录取的地方提供建议。

paragraphs.en: They would help draft his application, and if he got in, assist with immigration. They would do all of this for free. "I was sceptical," said Sam. "Like, why would you do that?"
paragraphs.zh: 他们会帮助他起草申请材料，如果他成功录取，还会协助办理移民手续。所有这些服务都是免费的。"我很怀疑，"萨姆说，"比如说，你为什么要那样做？"

paragraphs.en: The agent explained that they didn't need to charge students because the universities paid a commission. Other agencies kept calling, too. Sam (not his real name) spoke to half a dozen, all eager to handle his application.
paragraphs.zh: 中介解释说，他们不需要向学生收费，因为大学会支付佣金。其他中介机构也不断打来电话。萨姆（化名）与其中六家都谈过，它们都渴望处理他的申请。

paragraphs.en: Some immediately gave him a bad vibe. "It was all just for money, they wanted to get me admitted into any university at the fastest pace possible," he said. In the end he went with an agent from Edvoy, a large firm, who seemed to give him more frank advice.
paragraphs.zh: 有些机构立刻给他留下了不好的印象。"完全就是为了钱，他们想让我以最快的速度被随便哪所大学录取，"他说。最后，他选择了一家名为Edvoy的大型公司的中介，这位中介给他的建议似乎更坦诚。

paragraphs.en: The agent told Sam that his bachelor's degree in commerce from a small-town university did not hold much value, so he needed to be realistic about his prospects in the UK. Sam wanted to go into the process open-eyed. He signed up.
paragraphs.zh: 该中介告诉萨姆，他在一个小镇大学获得的商科学士学位价值不高，所以他需要对自己在英国的前景持现实态度。萨姆希望整个过程自己都能保持清醒。他签约了。

paragraphs.en: Each year, about 400,000 international students are granted study visas to the UK. A significant proportion do so with the help of education agents: middlemen paid by universities to find foreign students.
paragraphs.zh: 每年，大约有40万名国际学生获得赴英留学签证。其中很大一部分是在教育中介的帮助下实现的——这些中间人由大学付费来寻找外国学生。

paragraphs.en: In 2023, UK universities spent a total of £500m on education agents – but there is very little oversight of how these agents operate. In 2021, Priya Kapoor (not her real name) took a job working for StudyIn, a large education consultancy, in a major Indian city.
paragraphs.zh: 2023年，英国大学在教育中介上总共花费了5亿英镑——但对这些中介如何运作的监督却很少。2021年，普丽雅·卡普尔（化名）在印度一座大城市为大型教育咨询公司StudyIn工作。

paragraphs.en: It was her first job out of university. The pay was good, but she didn't know what to expect. What she found was something akin to a factory production line, where students were the product.
paragraphs.zh: 这是她大学毕业后的第一份工作。薪水不错，但她不知道会遇到什么。她发现就像工厂的生产线般，学生就是产品。

paragraphs.en: The first part of the production line were the agents – sometimes referred to as admissions consultants – who brought in students and acted as their main point of contact. Inevitably, Kapoor said, their advice on where to apply was often coloured by which institutions paid the highest commission.
paragraphs.zh: 生产线的第一部分是中介——有时被称为招生顾问——他们招来学生并充当主要联系人。卡普尔说，不可避免地，他们提供的建议往往受到那些支付最高佣金院校的影响。

paragraphs.en: This is widely accepted to be the case across agencies. "Whichever college pays more gets more students. It's not rocket science," said Prabakaran Srinivasan, an independent education agent based in Tamil Nadu, who is critical of unethical practices in the sector.
paragraphs.zh: 这在业内很普遍。"哪所大学付的钱多，就能得到更多学生。这不是什么高深的事，"位于泰米尔纳德邦的独立教育中介普拉巴卡兰·斯里尼瓦桑说，他批评该行业的不道德行为。

paragraphs.en: (Universities are not legally required to disclose what they pay to agents, and many treat details of rates as commercially sensitive information, sometimes refusing freedom of information requests on this basis.)
paragraphs.zh: （法律并不要求大学披露他们付给中介的佣金，许多大学将费率细节视为商业敏感信息，有时以此为由拒绝信息公开请求。）

paragraphs.en: Next in the chain was Kapoor's team, which was responsible for the applications. Her job title was "statement of purpose editor" and her role was to interview students about their life and use that information to write personal statements on their behalf. To pay their fees, most students she spoke to planned to take out huge loans, often secured against their parents' homes or agricultural land.
paragraphs.zh: 流程的下一环是卡普尔的团队，负责处理申请。她的职位是"个人陈述编辑"，职责是采访学生的生活经历，并利用这些信息代他们撰写个人陈述。为了支付学费，她接触过的大多数学生都计划借大笔贷款，通常是以父母的房子或农业用地作为抵押。

paragraphs.en: They did so on the assumption that after graduation, they would earn enough to pay back the loan. "They had no idea about sponsorship, no idea about visas. They just thought, 'I'll go there and I'll get a job,'" Kapoor told me.
paragraphs.zh: 他们这样做是假设毕业后能挣到足够的钱来偿还贷款。"他们对资助一无所知，对签证也一无所知。他们只是想，'我去那里，然后就能找到工作，'"卡普尔告诉我。

paragraphs.en: From what she saw, admissions consultants rarely enlightened them. "Agents do anything to avoid further questions," she said. "The attitude was: you're just another application to me, and I have targets to complete."
paragraphs.zh: 据她所见，招生顾问很少会给他们启发。"中介为了不再被追问，什么事都做得出来，"她说。"他们的态度是：你对我来说只是又一个申请，而我有指标要完成。"

paragraphs.en: To an extent, Kapoor could understand this mentality: the pace of work was frenetic. As January deadlines approached, she was writing up to 20 applications a day. She had to prioritise.
paragraphs.zh: 在某种程度上，卡普尔能理解这种心态：工作节奏太疯狂了。随着一月截止日期的临近，她每天要写多达20份申请。她必须分清主次。

paragraphs.en: The better the university, the more time she took. As a rule of thumb, Russell Group applications got about half an hour. The lower-ranked universities that made up the vast majority of Kapoor's workload got, on average, 15 minutes each.
paragraphs.zh: 大学越好，她花的时间就越多。根据经验，罗素集团的申请大约需要半小时。构成卡普尔绝大部分工作量的低排名大学，平均每所只花15分钟。

paragraphs.en: "Some of them weren't the best, but nobody cared as we knew they'd get through," she said. "Every day I did about five applications for Coventry and I knew all the students would get in."
paragraphs.zh: "有些申请不是最好的，但没人在意，因为我们知道它们会被通过，"她说。"每天我要做大约五份考文垂大学的申请，我知道所有学生都会被录取。"

paragraphs.en: At Coventry University, 42% of students are international; it spent almost £45m on agent commissions in 2023-24.
paragraphs.zh: 其中42%的学生是国际学生；该校在2023-24年度花费了近4500万英镑用于中介佣金。

paragraphs.en: A spokesperson for the university strongly disputed Kapoor's account of their admissions practices, saying it was "far removed from the truth" and stated that only 55% of applicants receive and accept offers.
paragraphs.zh: 考文垂大学的一位发言人强烈反驳了卡普尔对其招生做法的描述，称其"与事实相去甚远"，并表示只有55%的申请人收到并接受了录取通知。

paragraphs.en: When asked for further details, such as the percentage who simply receive an offer rather than receive an accept, they referred me back to their previous statement.
paragraphs.zh: 当被问及进一步的细节，例如仅仅收到录取通知（而非收到并接受）的百分比时，对方让我参考他们之前的声明。
